summary.headline: IMFA Q1 FY27 posted record revenue and profit: output rose to ~80,000 t from ~65,000 t average, blended realisation just under INR120,000/t, FY27 volume guidance trimmed to ~380,000 t.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the highest-ever quarter for both revenue and profitability, driven by firm ferrochrome prices and tonnage from the KNR-2 acquisition. Production was about 80,000 t against a prior average of about 65,000 t per quarter. Management trimmed FY27 volume expectations to about 380,000 t from 400,000 t, citing transformer loading limits and a gas cleaning plant (GCP) that needs work at KNR-2. KNR-1 first furnace tapping is expected around the third week of August, with a second furnace by end-September/early October. Management guided that Q2 realisations would be broadly similar with a slight correction, and Q2 volume only marginally higher as ferrochrome inventory is built.

financial_highlights.value: INR281 per ton (as cited by analyst on Q1)
Q4 MTM hit of INR32 crore absent in Q1; forex gain booked in Q1

segments.name: Ferro alloys (ferrochrome)
segments.commentary: Q1 volume ~80,000 t vs ~65,000 t average; ~95% exports, mainly to the Far East; domestic ~19% of sales. Expected run-rate of ~120,000-125,000 t/month once all furnaces stabilise in Q4.

segments.name: Captive chrome ore mines
segments.commentary: Chrome ore sourced from captive mines is the largest input and is described as insulated from ore price moves. Stockpile of ~6 lakh t built for next year's additional capacity needs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production revised to ~380,000 t (from 400,000 t indicated earlier) due to transformer and GCP constraints at KNR-2.
FY28 production guided at 475,000-500,000 t; capacity described as a little more than 0.5 million t post Kalinganagar.
Q2 FY27: realisations broadly similar to Q1 with slight correction; volume marginally higher as ferrochrome stock is built.
KNR-1 first furnace expected to tap around third week of August 2026; second furnace by end-September/early October 2026.
Full benefit of Kalinganagar expected from Q4 FY27 once KNR-2's 4 furnaces and KNR-1's 2 furnaces run at higher load.
Management indicated margin uplift of INR1,500-2,000/t once KNR-1 and KNR-2 stabilise at ~500,000 t; no formal per-ton EBITDA guidance.
KNR-2 50,000 t furnace: environmental clearance clarity expected in 3-4 months; additional INR15-20 crore approved in budget.
capex_capacity: KNR-1 greenfield: first furnace refractory heating underway, first tapping expected third week of August 2026; second furnace by end-September/early October.
KNR-2 (acquired): 4 furnaces switched on in March 2026, but loading restricted; 2 sets of transformers plus a spare ordered, to replace doubtful transformers in Q2-Q3 FY27.
Power constraint at KNR-2 cited as ~6-7 MW lower loading plus ~15 MVA load limit; gas cleaning plant work pending to meet emission norms.
Renewable power contract with JSW Energy: corridor available since June, power flow expected August; ~INR1 crore per month benefit indicated.
KNR-2 furnace of 50,000 t awaiting environmental clearance; expected operational around mid-2027, with clarity in next 3-4 months.
Board approved an additional INR15-20 crore budget for KNR-2 environmental and related work.
demand_pricing: Ferrochrome prices at recent highs; management expects Q2 prices broadly similar with slight correction; no Q3/Q4 price guidance.
Met coke prices up a little (currency depreciation in Colombia, high ferrochrome prices); impact expected in Q3 rather than Q2.
Chinese/South African supply: Eskom special tariff ($0.62/unit cited) lifting South African output; management expects chrome ore reallocation to offset, but flagged possible glut risk.
Global stainless steel production growth ~2.5-3% per management.
Domestic demand: management expects Indian ferrochrome demand to grow; duty protection only ~2-3%, so domestic and export pricing near parity.
FACOR capacity expansion (145,000 t to 500,000 t by FY28) noted by analyst; management declined to comment on FACOR plans.
West Asia crisis: no direct impact (no imports or sales to West Asia); freight costs up modestly but offset by prices.

qa_highlights.question: Expected Q2 volume, at least 90,000 t given KNR-2 running at optimum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers; output to rise further, but some ferrochrome stock build (17,000-18,000 t needed at higher output) will limit the increase. Q2 volume increase expected to be marginal.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 EBITDA a base for the coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: No definitive statement. Prices similar in Q2 with slight correction, offset by a slightly higher tonnage; Q3 and Q4 to see much larger tonnage.

qa_highlights.question: Has the KNR-1 and KNR-2 benefit reached EBITDA per ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Not much yet; ramp-up inefficiencies (power consumed without output). Full benefit expected from Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Per-ton EBITDA trajectory and whether FY27 volume will be 360-380k t?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 380,000 t for FY27; per-ton EBITDA guidance not given, with margin uplift of INR1,500-2,000/t expected once 500,000 t is reached smoothly.

qa_highlights.question: Met coke and cost per ton outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Chrome ore cost is insulated via captive mines; met coke has risen modestly, with the impact seen in Q3. Royalty increases a potential risk.

qa_highlights.question: Coke and ore consumption per ton of ferrochrome?
qa_highlights.answer: About 0.65 kg of coke and about 2.5 t of chrome ore per ton of ferrochrome.

risks_watch: KNR-2 transformer replacement (Q2-Q3) and GCP work; any further load restrictions would cut the 380,000 t FY27 target.
KNR-2 50,000 t furnace environmental clearance timing, expected mid-2027.
Ferrochrome price correction in Q3-Q4 as South African supply recovers; management would not give visibility.
Possible domestic supply additions (FACOR expansion) and domestic pricing pressure.
Met coke price rise and currency movements (Colombia) feeding into costs from Q3.
Forex MTM volatility on export hedges (Q4 FY26 precedent of INR32 crore hit).
key_quotes: this is a real breakthrough quarter where in terms of both revenues as well as profitability, it's the highest ever.
we're toning down the guidance a little bit for FY27.
we generally don't give any guidance with regard to tonnage, but given that there is so much happening in terms of greenfield, in terms of the acquisition, etc., so we had given some indications.
I advise investors not to look at IMFA from quarter-on-quarter basis or what we will achieve this quarter or next quarter.
we definitely don't give a guidance for Q3 and Q4.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term ramp (KNR-1 and KNR-2 volumes, ~120,000-125,000 t/month by Q4), but cautious and often evasive on near-term numbers: management declined per-ton EBITDA guidance, Q3-Q4 price visibility, and Q2 volume figures, and repeatedly steered investors to a longer-term trajectory. It was openly transparent about trimming FY27 volume to ~380,000 t because of transformer, GCP and power constraints at KNR-2.
